## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized flannel moth characterized by its fuzzy yellow to golden body and soft, woolly wings, giving the adult a plush appearance. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, parks, yards, gardens, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where host plants such as blueberries, oaks, and plums occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plant foliage and should not be handled because flannel moth larvae have hidden stinging spines that can cause painful skin irritation.
